name: eval-inventory
summary:
Most of what the hillclimb method needs already exists, split across three places. The pieces do not yet connect into a loop that can roll a live change back.

(1) The binary ships the method itself. CC 2.1.293 (the production pin; `bin/cc-claude-bin --print` resolves to ~/.claude-293) bundles the claude-api skill. Its subcommand table includes `build-eval` and `hillclimb`, next to cost-optimize, migrate and managed-agents-onboard. It also bundles shared/evals/{build-eval,eval-audit,cost-hillclimb,eval-hillclimb}.md, report/runner-scaffold.mjs, build-report-lite.mjs and SCHEMA.md (measured: `grep -a -o` on bin/claude.exe found 7x build-eval, 20x hillclimb and 2x each guide path). ~/.claude/skills/claude-api does not exist; the skill lives only inside the binary. I extracted read-only copies to /tmp/lev-design/eval-inventory/ (read at byte offsets with python, guides unpacked with zstd): eval-hillclimb.md 338 lines, eval-audit.md 204, build-eval.md 235, cost-hillclimb.md 442, schema.md 339, runner-scaffold.mjs 602, build-report-lite.mjs 488 (line counts measured with `wc -l`).

(2) The repo's best offline A/B harness is the token-efficiency gate (docs/research/token-efficiency-2026-09-23/eval/harness/). It has a decision rule written before any result was read, ABBA ordering, accounts kept out of the arm comparison, blind dossiers, failures classed from error text only, power and sample-size calculators, and a judge workflow. Smaller recipes elsewhere supply a sealed holdout split, calibration anchors re-judged in each panel, and an isolation recipe that runs on the subscription.

(3) The live telemetry is in place: four shadow logs plus the meter history, cc-idle-cache-readout with an ACCEPT line, and cc-quota-price, which turns tokens into percentage points of the meter.

House kill-switch convention: an env var CC_<NAME> read with a default, `[ "${CC_X:-on}" = off ] && exit 0` (older hooks use `${CC_X:-1} = 0`). The lever hooks use a mode default, `${CC_X:-shadow}`, and only "off" has a meaning so far. A switch reaches only NEW sessions. None is set in the live settings env (measured: 0 CC_* keys among the 13 env keys in ~/.claude/settings.json).

House one-command rollback for a settings registration: every c10 migration copies settings.json to ~/.claude/backups/<name>-<N>-<ts>/ and prints the backup path; batch runs undo with `bash scripts/c10-batch.sh --rollback <backup-dir>`. For code, rollback is a forward git revert landed with /ship, after which deploy-live advances. deploy-live never rolls the live layer back. postland auto-revert fires only on test reds, never on a telemetry regression.

items.name: Pre-registered A/B decision rule + statistics (reuse as the accept rule's engine)
items.detail: The PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE rule was written before any result was read. Primary metric: Wilcoxon on paired units. Guardrails: Fisher, with a Newcombe 95% CI lower bound held above a margin. The file also has wilson(), newcombe(), n_needed() and paired() helpers. Swap in the 'train up + test flat -> revert / both up -> keep' rule; the statistics carry over unchanged. Needs scipy.

items.name: Power / noise-floor calculator
items.detail: Computes exactly how many runs per arm a true tie needs to clear a margin, using agg.py's newcombe(); makes no model calls. Reuse it to show that the noise floor sits below the smallest improvement we act on.

items.name: Scheduler: ABBA order, accounts kept out of the arm comparison, quota stop, plumbing re-queue
items.detail: Runs ABBA ABBA AB per task. Each block runs entirely on one account, so the account never becomes an arm (matches the never-use-accounts-as-arms rule). Pauses an account at STOP_PCT 85. Re-queues quota, auth and timeout failures (max 3 attempts) and never counts them as arm failures.

items.name: Plumbing check: failure classes from error text, blind dossiers
items.detail: Classes each failure as quota, auth, timeout or other from the error text only, never from spend. Dedupes usage. Rewrites run paths and redacts anything that names the arm, so the dossier stays blind.

items.name: Per-run isolation for headless agent runs
items.detail: Gives each run a fresh fixture with its own bare origin, a private TMPDIR, and private per-run backlog/IDL stores, so eval runs cannot pollute the real ~/.claude stores. Trap: CLAUDE_BIN defaults to ~/.claude-280, so it must be overridden to the 293 pin.

items.name: Blind LLM judge workflow + seeded shuffle + keys kept apart
items.detail: One judge per task reads only the dossiers and a rubric of checkable items (rubrics.json, rubrics-heldout.json), returning success, items[], quality and harmful. Dossiers are shuffled with a seed, and the arm appears only in the keys/ files. Gap: the agent() call sets no model, so the judge runs on the session model, the same model under test.

items.name: Gate record and re-gate precedent
items.detail: A full worked verdict record (F1/F2, re-gate, rounds 3-4, R4.5 extension) in the house format: table, test, conviction. F2's 10 briefs have answers computed by code (harness/f2/setup.sh, workflow.js) and can re-gate workflow-lean for D2.

items.name: Sealed holdout split recipe
items.detail: Deterministic split, holdout when sha1(id)%5==0. Holdout numbers print only with --split holdout --unseal. A ready train/test split for transcript-sourced cases (seed it per round).

items.name: Judge self-consistency / drift anchors, multi-judge panel, paired sign test
items.detail: Calibration anchors are re-judged in every panel, labels are re-shuffled per judge, the panel has 3 judges, and paired.py runs exact McNemar/sign tests. run-arms.sh is the isolation recipe that works on the subscription (--tools "", --setting-sources "", neutral cwd), since --bare refuses OAuth.

items.name: Bundled claude-api build-eval / hillclimb guides, runner scaffold, report builder
items.detail: The /claude-api subcommands build-eval and hillclimb exist in 2.1.293. The scaffold gives the state layout .claude/hillclimb/<flow>/{_state.json, baseline/, vN/, results.jsonl, errors.jsonl, traces/<id>_rep<k>.json, change.md}. It also has --variant, --reps and --timeout-s, refuses to run a harness whose sha no human approved (--approve-harness), and asserts the served model. runCase is an API-client stub (scaffold :149-150) and must be adapted to a `claude -p` call, since no API key is set. SCHEMA.md defines train/val/test SplitScore with a 'significant/within noise' flag. The guides were extracted read-only.

items.name: Price list as code (tokens -> weekly pp) + telemetry design laws
items.detail: cc-quota-price dedupes on message.id (keeping the max output_tokens), fits tokens against the meter, and has --json, --census and --selftest. USAGE_TELEMETRY_100P §3.1-3.3 defines the layers: L1 tokens, L2 account-utilization.jsonl, L3 the join. Laws: report against window phase, abstain rather than impute, one renderer (claude-accounts --readout). §0 forbids any headline shaped as quality per token and rejects any quality cost, so quality must stay a hold guardrail, never part of a ratio.

D2: a4c54d1744d1--cost.py (distinct requestId, max usage), gaps.py, split3.py. D3: c0f9d5368147--turns.py, fit_tier.py. D4: 3df527edd333--grade.py, replay_pred.py, deny_followups.py. There are ~60 more under decisions-2026-10-24/scripts/. These are the eval set and grader for the transcript-sourced eval.

items.name: House per-hook kill switch (mode tri-state for levers)
items.detail: Convention: `[ "${CC_X:-on}" = off ] && exit 0` (older form `${CC_X:-1}` = 0). Lever hooks default to shadow: CC_IDLE_KEEPALIVE (shadow|off), CC_SUBAGENT_LONG_BASH (shadow|off, also gated at the validate-bash pipe), CC_IRS (on|off; the IRS block also takes CC_IRS_K, CC_IRS_K2 and CC_IRS_N_MIN), CC_WORKFLOW_SHADOW (!=off). A switch takes effect in NEW sessions only. Adding an enforce value (e.g. CC_X=enforce|shadow|off) extends the existing pattern. Setting a switch fleet-wide means editing the settings env, which is c10, an operator step.

Its header comment lists three ways back: delete the entry, set CC_X=off, or restore the backup. The batch runner records a MANIFEST and undoes with `bash scripts/c10-batch.sh --rollback <backup-dir>`. Rule 4 of the migrations README: back up before you clobber.

items.name: Code rollback path: /ship kill switches, postland auto-revert, deploy-live anti-rollback
items.detail: /ship's env kill switches: SHIP_LAND_LANE=v1, POSTLAND_AUTOREVERT=off, POSTLAND_VERIFY=off, and launchctl bootout of com.claude.deploy-live. postland-verify auto-reverts a bisected culprit only on a reproducible test red. deploy-live never rolls back ('rolling the live layer back is an operator decision'), so reverting a lever's code is a forward revert landed through /ship.

items.name: Monotone baselines (ratchets) for never-regress checks
items.detail: The land gate uses ratchet and baseline files. The pattern could hold an accepted lever's measured savings as a floor.

items.name: Repo rules that bind the design
items.detail: Arms must differ in ONE thing, and the precondition should be asserted, not assumed (:36). Counter lag moves arm N's cost into arm N+1's window, so settle with a no-new-calls hold before reading the meter (:146). Classify a quota fault by its error text, not by its spend (:80). A gate's P(pass) must rise with n (:39). A parse failure is a verdict, not noise (:239). An agent definition is cached at session start, so A/B it headless (:231).

gaps: Nothing assigns arms at random per session: no canary, cohort or randomize logic was found in hooks/bin/lib/scripts (grep; the only hits are cc-lr reconciler cohorts, which are unrelated). D1-D4 need a new hash-of-session-id arm, e.g. sha1(sid)%2, logged in every shadow row, with the kill switch as the always-on control.

The quota meter is too coarse for any single lever. weekly_pct was an integer in 5000/5000 of the latest account-utilization.jsonl rows, and wire_7d_util (non-null in 218 of them) moves in 0.01 steps, i.e. 1 pp (both measured with a python scan of `tail -5000`). A per-wake effect of about 0.006 pp (TESTS.md) is far below that. Per-lever impact must be priced from transcript tokens with cc-quota-price or the fixed weights; the meter is only a fleet-level sanity check, read after a hold that lets counter lag settle.
Native OTel (the USAGE_TELEMETRY_100P L1 layer) is not enabled: no TELEMETRY/OTEL key in the ~/.claude/settings.json env (python key scan). Enabling it would be a settings edit, i.e. c10.

In the token-efficiency harness the judge model equals the tested model: judge-workflow.js:52-54 sets agentType workflow-lean and effort but no model. That harness also has no judge self-consistency check (grep for kappa, agreement and re-judge in harness/ found only regate-probe-judge.py:9, which says it does not re-judge). The codex-probe judge.py anchors pattern would have to be ported.
The F1 gate has no train/test split (shard-hillclimb.md:30-35). No eval in the repo yet splits transcript-sourced cases for D1-D4.

No auto-revert or alarm exists for a telemetry regression. postland auto-revert covers test reds only, and deploy-live refuses rollbacks. Rolling back a lever means flipping its env kill switch or restoring a c10 backup, both operator steps, or a forward revert through /ship.

The bundled runner-scaffold.mjs runCase is an API-client stub (lines 149-150). The accounts have no API key, and --bare refuses OAuth (shard-hillclimb.md:19-22), so the scaffold must be adapted to `claude -p` using the run-arms.sh isolation recipe.

There is no baseline with a CI or a noise floor for the shadow metrics yet. The logs are less than a day old: idle-keepalive 593 rows and subagent-long-bash 642, all from 2026-10-24, idle-recycle-shadow 107, workflow-lean-shadow 16 (`wc -l`). The 7-day shadow week is the baseline window.

Besides the extracted guides, /tmp/lev-design/eval-inventory/ holds scratch frame0-9.zst files from the extraction; nothing was removed. No other writes.

name: telemetry-inventory
summary:
I inventoried about 20 stores and readers. Nothing in the fleet can attribute quota to a treatment arm: no store has an arm field, and no per-session arm assignment exists anywhere (grep for CC_ARM/CC_EXP/treatment in bin, hooks, scripts and lib found none; cc-instructions-variant's own header says "per-session A/B arms run only in /tmp fixtures").

Session attribution is good. Every shadow log, land.log (667 of 711 ship-land rows in 7 days carry a sid), claude-crashes.jsonl (679 of 679), permission-denied, validate-bash-decisions and backlog done rows (276 of 291 carry closedSession) key on the session id.

Quota itself is metered only per account. account-utilization.jsonl holds whole-number percents that round up and stop at 100, sampled about every 7.4 minutes (median gap 444 s, p95 551 s over 7 days; measured with /tmp/lev-design/telemetry-inventory/au.py). Several dozen sessions share one account. If arms are randomized by session, both arms bill the same account meter, so the meter cannot separate them. It can only check a per-session token-times-weights model (estimated by reasoning from the schema).

The closest per-session instrument is bin/cc-token-ledger. It dedupes on message.id, removes copies of the same message held under other accounts, and computes tool_err from is_error, with --by-arm and --by-agent-type views. But it prices in list-price dollars, not quota pp, its arm is the instructions variant per account, and it keeps nothing on disk.

Pipeline gaps I measured:
- cc-ctx-audit does not read ~/.claude-secondary/projects, the root that held all 3 of the 7 days' "Prompt is too long" transcripts (grep in wall.sh).
- `cc-ctx-audit --wall-hits --since 7d` did not finish in 240 s (rc 124).
- postland-verify fired 2 times and gave up "lock-held" 94 times in October (grep of idl.jsonl), so red/green after a land is mostly unmeasured.
- handoffs.jsonl has no successor session id and holds only about 3 days (first row 2026-10-21).
- Nothing detects operator re-asks or corrections, or successor rework.
- D4's target class has no rows: in the subagent log's v2 rows, all 36 poll-loop rows are exempted by their inner timeout, and would_deny_class=poll-loop appears 0 times (shadow.py).

Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/lev-design/telemetry-inventory/ (au.py, shadow.py, wall.sh, plus the failed run's wall7d.json and wall7d.err). Nothing outside that folder was written.

items.name: account-utilization.jsonl (quota meter history)
items.detail:
What it measures: per account, the endpoint session_pct (5h), weekly_pct and fable_pct; k, plus where k came from and the native k census; reset times; the wire_5h/7d util fields; the stale flag and auth state. 59,978 rows since 2026-08-10, in 4 schema generations, 0 parse errors (au.py).

Cadence: written only when some caller triggers a fresh claude-accounts sweep, at most once per 300 s. Measured over 7 days: median gap 444 s, p95 551 s, and 2 gaps over 30 min totalling 4.3 h. All four accounts are written in the same sweep, so the gaps are the same for all four.

Coverage gaps (7-day counts per account from inline python):
- weekly_pct is always a whole number (0 non-integer rows out of 59,960); it rounds up and stops at 100.
- Rows at 100: next 15, next2 65, next3 78, next4 22, of 1,364 each.
- The wire 7d field is present on only 17 / 122 / 79 / 23 rows.
- stale=true on 958-1,368 rows per account over all time.

Attribution: account only, no session id. Treatment arm: not possible, because arms randomized by session share an account's meter.

items.name: cc-quota-price (--census, and the fit)
items.detail:
Reader only. --census walks the four real transcript roots and dedupes on message.id; output is the maximum over a message's records. The fit is non-negative least squares of the change in weekly_pct per (account, 6 h bucket) on output + cache_creation + input. cache_read is reported as a bound, never as a fitted coefficient.

The census record keeps {ts, acct, model, the 4 token classes} and drops the file path and session id, so it cannot attribute to a session. Its 'seen' set spans all roots, so a message copied under another account is credited to the first root walked (next before next2 and so on), not the one that wrote it first. cc-token-ledger keeps the earliest file instead.

Its own docstring says agent output is a lower bound: 11.1% of responses on 2.1.280 never got a final record. That biases Workflow- and subagent-heavy arms (D2, D4).

Use here: checking the weights against the meter (read 0.0067 / write 0.245 / output 0.404). It cannot be the scorer.

items.name: cc-token-ledger (per-task cost, not in the brief's list)
items.detail:
Reader. Groups a main session with its subagents and workflow agents into one task. It removes copies held under other accounts (keeps the earliest file), imputes missing agent output, computes tool_results and tool_err from is_error (:260, :460), and has --task <sid>, --by-arm and --by-agent-type views.

Gaps:
- It prices list-price dollars, not quota pp.
- --by-arm reads ~/.claude/autonomy/instruction-variants.jsonl per account and time (:697-733), not a per-session arm.
- It writes nothing to disk.

It is the natural base for a per-session pp-and-guard scorer. TEST_PLAN.md (docs/research/token-efficiency-2026-09-23) already names it as the primary per-session instrument.

Plumbing defects (measured):
- DEFAULT_ROOTS lists ~/.claude, ~/.claude-tertiary and ~/.claude-quaternary, but not ~/.claude-secondary/projects. That root is a real directory, not a symlink, with 2,000 transcripts modified in 7 days. It held all 3 of the 7 days' wall-hit transcripts; the other roots had 0 (wall.sh plus a find|grep on quaternary).
- `cc-ctx-audit --wall-hits --since 7d --json` was killed at 240 s (rc 124), still in its per-file realpath loop (wall7d.err).
- The autonomy EVENTS/WINDOWS paths are fine: all five config dirs show the same 5,139 / 4,667 rows, i.e. one shared store.

items.name: land.log (ship-land + land-lock rows) and gate-red-census / land-speed-census
items.detail:
ship-land rows carry sid, verify, exit, gate_scope, smoke, net, red, total_s and gate_s. Measured over 7 days: 711 ship-land rows, 667 with a sid. Exit codes: 0 296, 42 208, 6 153, 143 24, 5 23, 11 5, 75 1.

Tool-less rows (exit 0 300, 42 208, -1 119, 5 2, 75 1) are lock wait/hold records written by land-lock.sh. Some of their exit values match ship-land's counts exactly (42 208 in both), so they appear to echo the land's exit code. They are not extra lands.

Readers: scripts/gate-red-census.sh and scripts/land-speed-census.py (it has --compare ISO for before/after).

Can attribute to a session: yes. To an arm: no field. Gap: what each exit code means is not mapped to failed land versus refusal versus nothing to land, so a 'failed lands' guard needs that mapping first.

items.name: postland-verify (IDL row + stamps)
items.detail:
The suite run after each land. idl.jsonl gets one fired or abstained row per call, keyed by commit sha with no session id. In October: 94 abstained (lock-held) versus 2 fired (grep of idl.jsonl).

Stamps under ~/.claude/autonomy/postland/stamps/<tree>.json carry the verdict, failing tests, run_s and retries. Over 14 days: cut 41, red 29, green 12, hung 2 (inline regex over those files).

Attribution: by commit only. A session can be joined through the land.log head field. No arm. Gap: red-gate rate as a guard is mostly unmeasured, because the post-land run rarely produces a verdict.

items.name: cc-idle-cache-readout
items.detail:
Reader over idle-keepalive.jsonl and subagent-long-bash.jsonl. For each account and day it reports gaps, would-wakes, saves, unneeded and insufficient wakes, net pp (low..high range) and timer coverage, plus the subagent rule priced by class against the 0.2% ACCEPT bar.

Run with --days 1 (measured): next 438 gaps / 21 would-wakes / net +0.52..+0.54 pp; next2 39 / 2; next3 4 / 0; next4 98 / 2. Subagent narrowed rule: ACCEPT OVER the bar on next (0.50-0.64 pp/week) and next4 (0.71-0.90).

All of these pp are counterfactuals priced from the weights, not metered. It has no per-session view and no arm split, and its class table still keys on `why`.

gaps: ARM: nothing assigns or records a per-session treatment arm. No CC_ARM-style variable exists, and session-start-dispatch.jsonl and every shadow log lack an arm field. Since accounts must not be arms, the arm has to be assigned per session id: a deterministic hash of sid plus a salt is one option, which would also let the arm be recomputed for rows already logged (estimated: design inference). It must also be logged at SessionStart.

PP PER SESSION: the meter is per account, in whole percents that round up and stop at 100, sampled every 444 s (median), with dozens of sessions on one account (measured: au.py). Session-randomized arms share each account's meter, so pp per session can only be modelled: deduped tokens times the weights read 0.0067 / write 0.245 / output 0.404. The meter's role is to check that model (cc-quota-price fit residuals), not to compare arms (estimated: reasoning from the schema).

NO STORED PER-SESSION PP LEDGER: cc-quota-price --census drops the session id (bin/cc-quota-price:331-338). cc-token-ledger prices list-price dollars and writes nothing to disk. idle_gap prices only idle gaps. What is needed is one stored row per task: sid, account, arm, deduped tokens by class including subagent and workflow agents, pp at the weights, and imputed agent output.

CROSS-ACCOUNT COPIES: cc-quota-price credits a copied message to the first root it walks (bin/cc-quota-price:303-321), while cc-token-ledger keeps the earliest file. A per-session scorer must use the earliest-file rule. Agent output under-reads by about 11% on 2.1.280 (cc-quota-price docstring), which biases the D2 and D4 arms, since both act on agent traffic.

USEFUL-WORK DENOMINATOR: no per-session work unit is defined. Candidates that already carry a sid: ship-land exit 0 rows in land.log (667 of 711 rows have a sid), backlog done rows with closedSession (276 of 291 in 7 days), commits. Exit codes 42, 6 and 5 need meaning mapped before 'failed land' can serve as a guard.

OPERATOR RE-ASKS / CORRECTIONS: no detector exists. TEST_PLAN.md lists this guard against 'transcripts', read by hand. A grader is needed: a programmatic pre-filter on the operator's next prompt, then an LLM judge with a checkable rubric, run on a model other than the tested one.

SUCCESSOR REWORK and first-turn size (D1, G6): handoffs.jsonl has prev_sid but no successor sid, and holds only about 2.4 days (first row 2026-10-21). The idle-recycle shadow does not log the next operator prompt that G6 asks for. Rework is unpriced (W4).

PROMPT-TOO-LONG DEATHS: cc-ctx-audit does not read ~/.claude-secondary/projects (bin/cc-ctx-audit:72-74), where all 3 of the 7 days' wall transcripts were (measured: wall.sh grep). Its 7-day run did not finish in 240 s (rc 124). This is the brief's plumbing-check failure: an instrument that misses one account reads as 'no regressions'.

RED GATES: postland-verify gave up 'lock-held' 94 times and fired 2 times in October (grep of idl.jsonl), and its stamps are keyed by commit, not session. The 14-day verdicts were cut 41, red 29, green 12, hung 2, so the post-land red rate is mostly unmeasured.

STUCK SESSIONS: no per-session stuck ledger exists. cc-wedge-watch covers only panes that never produced a turn, never-stuck-gate is a gate rather than a log, and claude-crashes.jsonl records deaths only. A candidate signal is gaps left open past N minutes with work pending (the 1-day read-out reports 56 open gaps).
TOOL-ERROR RATE: computed only on demand by cc-token-ledger from is_error (:260, :460); nothing stores it per session. tool-batch-census.jsonl has no error field.

SHADOW COVERAGE: (1) the subagent log has 0 rows from next2 or next3. (2) Among its v2 rows, would_deny_class=poll-loop appears 0 times; all 36 poll-loop rows are exempted by their inner timeout, so D4's target population is empty. (3) The Workflow log has no account field and no outcome (run tokens, success, resubmit after block), and 0 resume rows. (4) Keepalive gap rows are still v1, without the busy and watcher fields. (5) The idle-recycle log has 0 tertiary rows, and the 200k field is on only 36 of 109 rows. Each shadow log records counterfactual predicates, not outcomes.

NOISE FLOOR: the four changes are estimated at about +4 to +11 pp/week fleet-wide, on a capacity of about 400 pp/week, i.e. 1-3% (estimated, from the decisions REPORT). The whole-percent account meter cannot resolve that within a week. CIs must come from bootstrapping over sessions on the modelled pp. The weight uncertainty (round-3 read range 0.0057-0.0076) has to be carried into each CI. No baseline with a CI exists yet.

name: noise-floor
summary:
I measured the noise floor of the candidate online metrics over 28 days (2026-09-26 to 10-24, America/Chicago days, 4 weeks). Sources: 23,375 transcript files (30.8 GB), 3,454 main sessions and 660,140 unique requests, plus account-utilization.jsonl and land.log. Everything is measured with scripts in /tmp/lev-design/noise-floor/scripts unless marked estimated.

Answer: no decision can be detected online by fleet outcome metrics, under either design.
- (a) A session-randomized 50/50 split over 7 days detects nothing smaller than about 31-118% (relative) on any metric. Restricted to the sessions each decision actually touches, it still needs 51-89%.
- (b) A before/after week comparison needs 42-123%.
- The decisions' expected effects are 0.35-2.8% of fleet usage (4-10% within the sessions they touch). The gap is 9 to more than 100 times. On top of that, the weekly values drift 13-20% per week on their own (for example fleet m1 went 10.1 -> 8.0 -> 8.0 -> 6.7), so a before/after comparison is confounded.

What does work online is randomizing per event instead of per session:
- **D3:** assign each idle gap of 55 min or more to wake or no-wake. MDE is 5.7 / 4.0 / 2.8 pp/week after 1 / 2 / 4 weeks, adjusting only for context at gap start. Adding the time the real next turn arrives as a second covariate brings it to 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.7, but that needs a check that the two arms are balanced on it. Expected effect is 3.9-5.1, so D3 is detectable.
- **D4:** assign each poll-loop call. MDE is 2.55 / 1.80 / 1.27 pp/week against 1.4-5.2 expected. One week catches the upper half of that range; the low end needs 4 weeks. A one-day trial can only check compliance (MDE about 6.7 pp/week, estimated by sqrt(7) scaling).
- **D1:** per-session MDE is 28.6 / 20.3 / 14.3 pp/week against 8-11, and no covariate helps (R2 0.00). It needs offline evals plus per-recycle accounting of the savings.
- **D2:** only 73 sessions in 28 days used Workflow, and the per-session MDE is 89% relative. It needs a paired offline eval.

The m4 quality guards only catch large regressions:
- tool errors: 31-41% in 7 days
- failed lands: about 73%
- prompt-too-long deaths: the baseline is zero, so the guard is a count alarm (3 or more main-session deaths in a week)

Use them as rollback tripwires, not as evidence of improvement.

Data files: /tmp/lev-design/noise-floor/summary.tsv (one row per metric and account) and /tmp/lev-design/noise-floor/event_level.out. Everything was read-only except /tmp/lev-design/noise-floor/.

items.name: Expected effects vs MDE, fleet designs
items.detail:
Expected effects as a share of about 400 pp/week (estimated): D1 2.8%, D2 1.3-2.8%, D3 1.1%, D4 0.35-1.3%.

Restricted to the sessions each decision touches (measured wpp/week of those sessions):

| Decision | Sessions touched (28 d) | Their wpp/week | Expected effect within them | Session A/A MDE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 (idle 15 min at 200k context or more) | 646 | 279 | 4.0% | 51% |
| D2 (sessions using Workflow) | 73 | 112 | 4.5-10% | 89% |
| D3 (gap of 55 min or more) | 560 | 256 | 1.8% | 53% |
| D4 (subagent poll loop) | 162 | 187 | 0.7-2.8% | 71% |

Cost is concentrated: the top 1% of sessions hold 31% of wpp and the top 10% hold 75%.

Verdict: no decision is detectable by a session-randomized 7-day split or a before/after week on m1-m3.

items.name: Event-level online designs
items.detail:
MDE at 80% power, in pp/week fleet, after 1 / 2 / 4 weeks (measured: eventmde.py, cuped.py, cuped_strict.py, d4events.py).

| Decision | Unit randomized | Events/week | MDE (1 / 2 / 4 wk) | Expected | Detectable online? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D3 | each main gap of 55 min or more | 906 | 5.7 / 4.0 / 2.8 adjusting for context at gap start (R2 0.11); 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.7 adding real-return timing (R2 0.94) | 3.9-5.1 | Yes: in 1 week if the timing covariate passes an arm-balance check, otherwise 2-4 weeks |
| D4 | each poll-loop call | 932 (82 with a gap over 300 s) | 2.55 / 1.80 / 1.27 (R2 0.06) | 1.4-5.2 | Upper half in 1 week; low end needs 4 weeks |
| D1 | first idle point of each session (15 min, 200k) | 162 | 28.6 / 20.3 / 14.3 (R2 0.00) | 8-11 | No, even at 4 weeks |
| D2 | Workflow sessions | about 18 | not measured per run | 5-11 | No |

A D4 one-day trial has an MDE of about 6.7 pp/week (estimated, sqrt(7) scaling), so it can only check compliance.

So D1 and D2 need offline evals:
- **D1:** compute the mechanical saving per recycle from the shadow-log counterfactual, then measure the side costs per recycle: the successor's first turn, rework, and replays of the wrong-action cases.
- **D2:** run lean against default as a paired eval on Workflow briefs taken from production, with a judge model different from the one tested.

items.name: Structural traps for the telemetry design
items.detail:
1. **Saturation.** 30 of 112 account-days spent time at 100% (about 223 account-hours; measured: meter.py). While an account is pinned, savings show up as more work rather than fewer pp, so raw pp/week cannot be the metric; use ratios.
2. **Drift.** Week-over-week drift (13-20% per week on m1 and m2) is larger than any decision's effect, so only concurrent randomized controls work.
3. **No per-arm meter.** The meter cannot be split between arms; arm outcomes must be priced from transcript tokens. Fleet calibration (meter/wpp 1.20-1.36 by week) is stable enough to convert wpp back to meter pp.
4. **Per-account metrics are unusable** (day CV around 1-2.5).
5. **D1 successors.** A recycle creates a new session, which must inherit its predecessor's arm, and the metric must be computed over the whole predecessor-plus-successor chain.

gaps: Prompt-too-long deaths are detected only from isApiErrorMessage records whose text is 'Prompt is too long'. Other ways a session dies of context (for example a failed autocompact) are not counted.

Tool errors per day are split across days by each file's share of requests (estimated), not by per-error timestamps. That smooths the daily series a little. 'Hook-related' means the string 'hook' appears in the first 400 chars of the error.
Weekly CVs rest on 4 weeks. The 90% CI on the SD runs from 0.62x to 2.92x the point estimate (chi-square, 3 df), so the before/after MDEs could be up to about 3x worse.
wpp uses the brief's weights for every request; uncached input is priced at the write weight (estimate); the 0.6% non-Opus requests are not reweighted. Meter pp includes the 4 mid-window resets to 0.

Session A/A permutation: sessions are assigned to a week by their first request, randomization is simple (not stratified by account), 1,000 repetitions per week, and it assumes no interference between sessions.

D3 event noise uses every main gap of 55 min or more, not the busy-scoped subset with the watcher skip. D4 per-call outcome is only the next request's cache write; deny and re-issue costs are not included. D2 per-run noise and the D1 side costs per recycle (successor first turn) were not measured.
Shadow logs hold only about 1 day of rows (subagent-long-bash 647, idle-recycle-shadow 109, idle-keepalive 609, workflow-lean-shadow 16) and were not used for the noise floor.

66 lands (56 with no sid, 10 with no matching session) count in fleet totals only. The commits metric covers claude-infrastructure only: every successful land's head and base resolved there, and no other repo was checked.
Read-only as briefed: no telemetry or hillclimbing harness was built; this measures noise only.

name: option-a-session-ab
design:
OPTION A: ONLINE A/B, RANDOMIZED BY SESSION LINEAGE, FOR D1-D4

0. BOTTOM LINE
Randomizing by session is right for assigning arms and for the guards, but it decides efficacy for only two of the four levers, and only with a covariate. All numbers below are measured with scripts in /tmp/lev-design/option-a-session-ab/, on the noise-floor key's 28-day data (2026-09-26 to 10-24), unless marked estimated.

- **Grouping inflates the noise.** When arms are assigned per session, all events of one session share an arm, and the A/A noise grows with it. The design effect (deff) is how many times the variance grows compared with randomizing each event (cluster_mde.py → cluster_mde.out, 400 A/A repetitions at a 50/50 split).
  - D3: deff 7.6-8.6. There are 6.5 gaps per session on average (median 2, max 121), and 906 gaps of 55 min or more per week. The unadjusted minimum detectable effect (MDE) is 16.66 / 12.02 / 8.82 pp/week after 1 / 2 / 4 weeks; randomizing per event would give 6.03 / 4.32 / 3.01.
  - D4: deff 27-37. There are 22.7 poll-loop calls per session (max 867). The MDE is 19.08 / 12.04 / 8.12 pp/week.
  - Adjusting for context alone does not help (D3 17.39 / 12.01 / 8.90).
- **A strong covariate measured the same way in both arms removes most of it.**
  - D3: adjust for context, a flag for an operator return at 3600 s or later, and their product. R² is 0.942 and the MDE falls to 1.53 / 1.05 / 0.75 pp/week (1.80 / 1.22 / 0.85 at a 25% treatment share) (cluster_mde_timing.py → .out).
  - D4: adjust for context, a flag for an external wait over 300 s, and their product. R² is 0.856 and the MDE falls to 3.01 / 1.91 / 1.41 (cluster_mde_d4wait.py → .out). The "external wait" is how long the waited-for condition took to come true. In the treatment arm it is the time from the first denied call to the first slice that exits with something other than 124, so it can be measured the same way in both arms.
  - Expected effects: D3 +3.9 to +5.1 (+4.49 for the watcher-skip variant); D4 +1.4 to +5.2.
- **D1 cannot be decided online.** It has 161 events a week. Its relative MDE is 56.5 / 35.6 / 26.9% for rest-of-session pp and 59.2 / 49.5 / 31.0% for pp per request; covariates change nothing (d1_perreq.py → .out). The expected effect is about 4% of the touched sessions' pp (estimated: 11.1 / 279 pp/week).
- **D2 cannot be decided online either.** The noise-floor key measured a per-session MDE of 89% on 73 Workflow sessions in 28 days.
- **So option A does two things.** (a) It is the assignment and guard instrument for all four levers. (b) It is the efficacy instrument for D3 (look at day 14) and D4 (look at day 28), using the covariate-adjusted per-event estimator. Efficacy for D1 and D2 comes from modelled per-event savings, with measured side costs and confidence intervals from a bootstrap over lineages, plus the offline evals. A guard tripwire can still revert any lever.
- **D4 may have nothing to act on.** Of 202 subagent-long-bash v2 rows (2026-10-24 19:55Z-23:33Z, inline python count), 0 are poll loops the deny would target; all 37 poll-loop rows are exempt by their inner timeout. If no target events arrive, the expected D4 verdict is MOOT.

1. ARM ASSIGNMENT
- **Unit: the lineage, not the bare session id.** A lineage is a predecessor and its recycle successors, plus every /clear or compact inside the same claude process. Successors must inherit their predecessor's arm (noise-floor trap 5). Subagents and workflow agents already carry the parent's session_id: the last 200 rows of subagent-long-bash.jsonl all have a sid inside the main transcript_path (inline python), and so does this run's own Workflow row.
- **How the lineage is resolved**, first match wins:
  - (i) env CC_LEVER_LINEAGE, exported into the successor by scripts/handoff-fire.sh hf_succ_stage;
  - (ii) the process cache ~/.claude/state/levers/proc/<claude-pid>-<lstart>, which covers clear and compact. The ppid field is already in session-start-dispatch.jsonl: 558 rows, 501 sids, 2026-10-19 to 10-24 (inline python);
  - (iii) the session's own sid.
  - The scorer repairs typed-relaunch successors offline by joining the handoffs.jsonl recycle rows to the next session start in the same pane within 120 s. It records lineage_src for every lineage.
- **Hash.**
  - u_L = int(sha256(salt_L + ":" + lineage)[:13], 16) / 16**13.
  - A session is in treatment for lever L only if mode_L == enforce and u_L < share_L. Otherwise it is control.
  - Each lever has its own salt, so the arms of the four levers are independent: a 2^4 factorial. D3 is analysed within the D1-control stratum first, and the D1×D3 interaction is reported.
  - Raising the share (0.25 to 0.5 to 0.9) keeps earlier treatment sessions in treatment.
- **Train/test split.** split = train if int(sha256(split_salt_L + ":" + lineage)[13:26], 16) % 2 == 0, else test. A fresh split salt is drawn each round. Both halves run at the same time, which a time split cannot give: weekly drift is 13-20% (noise-floor key).
- **Never by account.** The account is a blocking covariate only. A sample-ratio-mismatch (SRM) check runs on each account.
- **Arms are computed in shadow mode too.** The current shadow week therefore doubles as a free A/A baseline. Rows logged before this ships get their arm recomputed with lineage = sid.
- **Cache.**
  - ~/.claude/state/levers/arms/<sid> is a plain-text line (lineage=… src=… idle-recycle=control:r1 … split=train) that bash can read with builtins, so validate-bash needs no fork.
  - One row per session goes to ~/.claude/logs/lever-arms.jsonl.
  - The resolver is lazy, so any hook can mint the arm. It is also stamped at SessionStart by a new child of session-start-dispatch. Precedent: recycle-failed-inject.sh was added as a child with no settings edit.

- **Agent output is mostly imputed.** In the same 1-day run, subagent output was 112,559 tokens recorded against 2,170,057 after imputation, and workflow-agent output 3,050,653 against 9,997,138. So D2 and D4 are scored on the input-side classes, and output is reported separately as imputed.
- **Estimators.** All are intention-to-treat by assigned arm, using the regression y = a + τT + βx with a cluster bootstrap over lineages, stratified by account and arm (B = 2000). The CR1 standard error must agree with the bootstrap within 20%; that is the self-consistency check of the statistic.
  - D3: event = a main gap where the busy-scoped predicate holds at minute 55, evaluated in both arms. y = the wake turns' pp plus the first request after the real return.
  - D4: event = a target poll-loop call. y = pp from the call through the first request after the external wait, including slices and re-issues.
  - D1: modelled saving per recycle. The successor's actual later requests are re-priced at the predecessor's projected context, minus the measured re-prime, handoff and orientation turns.
  - D2: modelled saving per blocked slot. The per-slot prefix difference is measured in both arms, minus the deny round trip.

  - logged and recomputed arms disagree on more than 0.5% of rows;
  - any real project root is missing;
  - parse failures exceed 0.1% of rows (a parse failure is a verdict, not noise);
  - placebo-salt A/A runs read significant in more than 3 of the last 20 runs;
  - exposure (treatment events actually actuated / predicate true) is below 80%, for example a hook timeout letting the call through (D2 has a 5 s timeout);

5. ACCEPT/REVERT RULE (the blog's rule; δ_min is the smallest improvement acted on)
- **Per half (train, test), at a pre-registered look only:**
  - up = 95% CI lower bound > 0 and point ≥ δ_min;
  - down = CI upper bound < 0, or any guard tripped;
  - flat = otherwise.
- **Decision:**
  - down on either half → REVERT;
  - both up → KEEP: share goes to 0.9, a 10% control holdback stays, and the report gives test against control with CI;
  - train up, test flat → REVERT;
  - test up, train flat, or both flat → STALL: revert to shadow, run `failures --split train`, edit nothing in that round;
  - fewer than n_min events → INSUFFICIENT: go to the next pre-registered look, then MOOT or STALL.
  - A gain within noise is reported as "within noise" and never merged.
  - `cc-lever round-start` refuses enforce unless an aa row shows the per-half MDE at the look is at most δ_min, and the tick heartbeat is less than 2 h old.
- **Per-lever settings.** Per-half MDE is estimated as full × √2.

6. TRIPWIRES → AUTOMATIC REVERT
These are checked hourly on cumulative round data, intention-to-treat, within touched sessions.
- **T1 tool errors per 100 requests, hook denials excluded:** revert if the treatment/control ratio is 1.4 or more and the one-sided 99% lower bound is above 1. The 7-day session A/A MDE is 41%.
- **T2 prompt-too-long main-session deaths:** revert at 3 or more in the treatment arm within 7 days (p ≈ 0.04 at the baseline's upper bound), or at any such death within 2 turns of a lever actuation.
- **T3 failed lands per land:** exit codes mapped, exit 42 excluded; revert if the ratio is 1.5 or more and the 99% lower bound is above 1 (A/A MDE 73%).
- **T4 CRASH-class rows in claude-crashes.jsonl:** same rule as T3.
- **Lever-specific:**
  - D1: G6, after at least 10 recycles: median successor first turn above 10 requests, or rework above 10k tokens. Also the judged re-ask rate exceeding control by more than 10 points with the CI excluding 0.
  - D2: any block on a resume.
  - D3: any wake with busy=false, or after the gap ended.
  - D4: any /goal trip, or second denies above 5%.
- **On a trip:**
  - `cc-lever rollback <id> --auto` runs;

D1 and D2 efficacy is modelled, not measured: the online MDE for D1 is 56.5% relative at 1 week (d1_perreq.out) against about 4% expected, and 89% per session for D2. The CIs carry only the weight range and the sampling noise, not model error (for example, the projected growth of the predecessor's context). Their online evidence is mostly the guards.

Lineage carry has gaps. The typed-relaunch fallback in handoff-fire does not carry CC_LEVER_LINEAGE, and the offline pane+time join can mis-link chains. Chains with mixed arms bias D1 toward null. The plumbing check needs at least 95% agreement between successor and predecessor arms.

Sessions interfere through shared account quota. 30 of 112 account-days spent time at 100% (noise-floor meter.py), so savings in treatment sessions let control sessions on the same account do more work. Event-level outcomes are fairly robust to this; the per-arm pp per unit of work and the meter are contaminated, so they stay descriptive and are never compared between arms.

Agent output is mostly imputed on 2.1.293 (measured, cc-token-ledger --since 1d: subagent output 112,559 recorded vs 2,170,057 after imputation; workflow agents 3,050,653 vs 9,997,138). D2 and D4 are scored on the input-side token classes, so an effect on output would be invisible.

When a hook times out or is missing for an account (D2 has a 5 s timeout; registration is per config dir), a treatment session silently behaves as control. Intention-to-treat dilutes the effect; the exposure gate (80% or more) and the per-account SRM check are what catch it.

Peeking and optional stopping. Daily score rows invite early reads. Only pre-registered looks can yield KEEP, the tripwires use stricter one-sided 99% bounds, and an unseal before the look voids the round.

Operators will feel the D1 treatment (recycles in the middle of a conversation). Mitigations: share 0.25 in week 1, the G4 hold, the G6 tripwires, and the judged re-ask guard. The judge spends quota and has its own error, which the anchors and double-judging bound but do not remove.

Auto-revert depends on the hourly launchd tick, which needs an operator-run c10 step (migration 0079). Until it runs, cc-lever must refuse enforce. A control file that is unreadable must fail to shadow and must raise an alarm, so it cannot pass as healthy.

The factorial interaction between D1 and D3 (both act on idle gaps) can bias a pooled D3 estimate. The primary D3 analysis is within the D1-control stratum, and the interaction is reported with its CI.

The per-half MDEs (×√2) and the D4 one-day MDE (×√7) are scalings, not separate measurements. The A/A permutations used 400 repetitions, so each SD carries about 3.5% sampling error (estimated, 1/√(2R)). The source data is 4 weeks long, so the weekly variance itself is uncertain (noise-floor: chi-square 90% CI on the SD of 0.62x-2.92x).

Deviations: I ran read-only bin/cc-token-ledger --since 1d (44 s, 4 workers) to time a daily scan, and four new analysis scripts over the noise-floor key's data. All writes went to /tmp/lev-design/option-a-session-ab/. I made no repo, settings, hook or git changes.

name: option-c-staged-canary
design:
OPTION C: a staged canary for each lever (S0 shadow, then S1 10%, S2 50%, S3 100%). One scorer (cc-lever-score) and one auto-rollback daemon (cc-lever-guard), with the hillclimb running inside S2/S3.

ANSWER FIRST
The ladder works for all four levers as a way to limit exposure while checking safety. The measured noise floor decides which stages can also say whether a lever saves anything:
- No lever's savings can be read at 10%. MDE at 10% over 1 week (computed: python3 -I /tmp/lev-design/option-c-staged-canary/stage_mde.py, from the noise-floor worker's measured per-event SDs) is D3 9.5 pp/week (adjusted for context), D4 4.25 and D1 47.9. S1 therefore checks tripwires and compliance only, and it ends on an event count, not on a number of days.
- D3 is the one lever the canary can confirm online. Its 50% MDE is 5.7 / 4.0 / 2.85 pp/week after 1 / 2 / 4 weeks adjusting for context only. If the "time of the real return" covariate passes an arm-balance test, the MDE is 1.48 / 1.05 / 0.74. Expected effect: +3.9 to +5.1.
- D4 can be detected in principle (2.55 / 1.80 / 1.27 against +1.4 to +5.2), but its target class is empty today. I recounted ~/.claude/logs/subagent-long-bash.jsonl with inline python: 37 poll-loop v2 rows, all exempted by their inner timeout, and 0 rows with would_deny_class=poll-loop. So D4 must first pass a population gate, and it is expected to PARK.
- D1 can never be confirmed from fleet or session outcomes: its MDE is 14.4 pp/week at 4 weeks against +8 to +11 expected. Its net pp/week comes from chain accounting per recycle: a modelled counterfactual, calibrated against the control arm, minus side costs measured on each recycle. The canary supplies safety evidence only.
- D2 has about 18 Workflow sessions a week (73 in 28 days, measured). The canary gives it a compliance verdict. A cost verdict comes online only if the per-run log-cost SD is about 1.2 or less (estimated); otherwise it comes from the offline paired re-gate.

1. CONTROL PLANE
- Flag file ~/.claude/state/levers/flags.json, shared by all four config dirs through $HOME. Schema:
  {v:1, rev, updated_at, updated_by: "operator:cc-lever"|"guard:cc-lever-guard", levers:{D1..D4:{decision, stage: S0|S1|S2|S3, pct: 0|10|50|100, holdback, mode: shadow|live|off, salt, split_salt, params:{...}, params_id, candidate: null|{id, params, share, round, round_salt}, thresholds_sha, stage_started_at, trip: null|{id, at, rule, evidence, by, acked_at}}}}
- Effective pct is 0 unless all of these hold: mode=live, no un-acked trip, guard.heartbeat no older than CC_LEVER_DEADMAN_S=1800 (the dead-man switch), and no env override.
- Precedence, highest first:
  1. The existing hook kills (CC_IRS, CC_IDLE_KEEPALIVE, CC_SUBAGENT_LONG_BASH, CC_WORKFLOW_SHADOW =off) stop the hook entirely, as today.
  2. New CC_LEVER_ALL=off and CC_LEVER_D1..D4=off turn the treatment off but keep shadow logging. These reach new sessions only, and setting them fleet-wide is a c10 settings edit.
  3. flags.json takes effect at the next hook call in every session.
  4. The default is pct 0.
  A flags file that cannot be read gives pct 0 with flag_src=unreadable, never live.
- Writers:
  - cc-lever (operator) can raise or lower. A raise needs --confirm, plus the latest lever-score verdict ADVANCE for that lever and stage (or --override "<reason>"), plus a fresh heartbeat and no un-acked trip. It writes tmp+rename under flock (flags.lock), increments rev, and appends an audit row to lever-flags.jsonl.
  - cc-lever-guard can only lower: pct to 0 with mode=shadow, or mode=off on plumbing trips.
  - Raising is sign-off class. Migration 0080 adds permission "ask" rules for cc-lever stage, candidate, promote and ack.
- A trip latches. Releasing it is not the trip condition clearing ("release != !trip"). `cc-lever ack <trip_id> --reason .. --confirm` clears the latch without raising anything. A fresh `cc-lever stage` raises; it re-pins thresholds_sha, restarts the stage clock, and rotates the salt so the tripped cohort does not carry over.

2. ASSIGNMENT (never by account)
- Treatment: u = int(sha256(salt|unit_id)[:13],16)/16^13. A unit is treated iff u < pct/100 and it is not in the S3 holdback (u >= 1-holdback).
- The salt stays fixed across S1, S2 and S3, so the 10% cohort sits inside the 50% cohort, which sits inside 100%. No unit flips from treated to control.
- Hillclimb variant: v is drawn from round_salt; cand iff v < share, within the treated units only.
- Train/test split: s is drawn from split_salt over the session id; test iff s < 0.5, and the test half is sealed.
- Units:
  - D1: the lineage root session. A successor inherits its arm through ~/.claude/state/levers/lineage/<pane>.json.
  - D2: the session. A denied session learns, so per-script units would contaminate each other.
  - D3: one idle gap (sid:gap_start), with CIs clustered by session. This is finer than a session because session-level MDE (53%) cannot see a 1.8% effect.
  - D4: the subagent agent_id (a denied agent learns), with CIs clustered by session.
- Asserted, not assumed (any failure is a PLUMBING verdict):
  - SRM chi-square p >= 0.001;
  - arm independent of account, chi-square p >= 0.001;
  - params_sha constant within each (arm, variant) segment;
  - sessions that crossed a stage boundary are excluded from session-level intent-to-treat analysis.

3. LOGS AND SCHEMAS
A. ~/.claude/logs/lever-arms.jsonl: one row per ELIGIBLE decision in BOTH arms, written before the treatment acts:
   {v:1, ts, lever, decision, unit, unit_id, sid, agent_id, acct, hook, stage, pct_eff, flag_rev, flag_src: file|env-off|deadman|unreadable|default, arm: treat|ctrl|holdback, u, variant: inc|cand|null, variant_id, split, params_id, params_sha, thresholds_sha, eligible:true, elig:{lever predicate inputs}, acted, hook_ms}
B. kind=session rows in the same file, from hooks/lever-arm-start.sh (a SessionStart child):
   {v:1, kind:"session", ts, sid, acct, source, headless, lineage_root, lineage_src: self|lineage-file|none, arms:{D1:{arm,u}, D2:{arm,u}}, split, flag_rev}
C. lever-flags.jsonl: {ts, rev, by, lever, from:{stage,pct,params_id}, to:{...}, reason, verdict_ref}
D. lever-guard.jsonl: state changes plus one heartbeat row an hour:
   {ts, tick_ms, levers:{L:{state: OK|TRIP|NO-DATA|IDLE, rule, evidence, n}}, acted:[...]}
E. lever-score.jsonl: one row per lever per --write. Its fields match SCHEMA.md SplitScore:
   {ts, lever, stage, window, look, thresholds_sha, n:{treat, ctrl, train, test}, plumbing:{...}, effect:{per_event:{score, ci_lo, ci_hi, n, significant}, fleet_pp_week, realized_pp_week, read_range, meter_equiv}, guards:{g:{treat, ctrl, delta, ci_lo, ci_hi, breach}}, verdict}
F. lever-judge.jsonl: {ts, batch, lever, dossier_id, rubric_id, items:[{claim, pass}], label, judge_model, order_seed, anchor, batch_kappa, batch_void}
G. Additions to the existing shadow logs (version bumps, no change in behaviour):
   - idle-keepalive.jsonl gap rows v2: episode_id (the original idle start, carried across gaps a wake splits), ended_by: record|wake, wake_req, wake_tokens, plus the busy and watcher fields (gap rows are still v1). Wake rows v3: lever (D1|D3), arm, variant, unit_id, eligible, fired.
   - idle-recycle-shadow.jsonl v2:
     - prompt_sha and prompt_head (at most 200 chars of the operator prompt that ended the gap, which is G6's "next operator prompt"), plus arm and variant;
     - kind=recycle rows {sid, lineage_root, pane, ctx, fired_at, done, successor_sid, succ_first_turn:{requests, cw, cr, out}}, written at the successor's first Stop.
   - subagent-long-bash.jsonl v3: arm, variant, acted, msg_id, and kind=d4_follow rows {agent_id, follows_tuid, delay_s, compliant, same_sha, second_deny}.
   - workflow-lean-shadow.jsonl: acct, arm, variant, acted, and follows_deny {denied_sha, delay_s, edited, now_would_deny, marker_added}.
   - Rows A-F and the four shadow logs are added to rotation and to store-bounds. None of the four shadow logs is in either today (grep).

4. SCORER: bin/cc-lever-score (stdlib Python 3.9, read-only)
- Commands:
  - `cc-lever-score [score] [--lever D1|D2|D3|D4|all] [--window stage|7d|ISO..ISO] [--split pooled|train|test] [--unseal] [--json] [--write] [--boot 2000] [--seed 7]`
  - `guards [--json]`: the daemon's fast path. It scans no transcripts and is bounded to 60 s.
  - `aa [--reps 200]`: an A/A test on shadow and control rows with pseudo-salts. It gives the verdict rule's false-positive rate and the live noise floor per lever, and it is the scorer's self-consistency check.
  - `failures --lever L --split train`: treated events that did harm, grouped by programmatic cause with the pp lost per cause. It refuses `--split test`.
  - `report`: test versus baseline with CIs for each stage and each round. Gains within noise get a "within noise - not merged" badge.
  - `selftest`: planted-effect, A/A, SRM and account-leak fixtures.
- Pricing: wpp = ((input + cache_creation)*0.245 + cache_read*R + output*0.404) / 1e6.
  - R = 0.0067. Every CI is also computed at R = 0.0057 and R = 0.0076, and the union is reported.
  - D4 is also priced at a 5-minute write weight of 0.20.
  - Meter-equivalent = wpp x that week's fleet meter/wpp ratio (measured 1.20-1.36). Never use per-account ratios (0.84-3.24).
- Token accounting: dedupe on message.id, keeping the earliest file (import cc-token-ledger :108-:416 read-only). Assert that all four transcript roots were read, including ~/.claude-secondary/projects, which cc-ctx-audit misses. Report the share of imputed agent output per arm.
- Outcome per event:
  - D3: the wake turn(s) plus the first real request after the gap, per gap episode.
  - D4: the agent's next request plus the overhead of the deny and re-issue.
  - D2: the deduped cost of the run's workflow agents plus the deny round-trip, compared as a log ratio.
  - D1: chain accounting (section 6).
- Estimator: difference in means with CUPED. Covariates: D3 context at gap start, plus time to real return only if a KS balance test gives p >= 0.05; D4 context; D1 context at idle. The bootstrap resamples whole sessions (cluster bootstrap), stratified by account. Account is a stratum, never an arm.
  - Fleet pp/week at 100% = per-event delta x eligible events/week; realized pp/week = that x pct.
  - D3 results are also split by the session's D1 arm.
- Looks: savings are read only on days 7, 14 and 28 of S2, with Haybittle-Peto bounds (|z| >= 3.0 at the interim looks, 1.96 at the final). Guards are read continuously and can only revert.
- Verdicts: ADVANCE, HOLD, REVERT, PARK, PLUMBING, NOT-MERGED (inconclusive at the maximum dwell, which sends the lever back to S0).
- Plumbing block in every score:
  - parse errors (a parse failure is a verdict, not noise);
  - share of rows with flag_src not equal to file;
  - SRM;
  - arm-by-account independence;
  - join coverage per arm (PLUMBING if the arms differ by more than 3 points);
  - imputed-output share per arm (PLUMBING if more than 5 points apart);
  - hook-timing rc != 0 or near-timeout for the lever hooks;
  - the scorer's own runtime;
  - void judge batches.

5. GRADERS
- Programmatic graders come first:
  - every savings figure;
  - compliance (edited resubmit, re-issued as told, recycle completed);
  - G1: the successor sees a task-notification for a job its predecessor launched, or a RECYCLE row while a job was running;
  - G4: session_jobs.pending_question at fire time;
  - double wakes and denies on a resume.
- An LLM judge is used only for re-asks/corrections and D1 wrong actions: bin/cc-lever-judge.
  - A regex prefilter runs on the next operator prompt.
  - The judge itself is `claude -p --model sonnet --tools "" --setting-sources ""` in a neutral working directory (the run-arms.sh:9-13 recipe). The judge model is not the Opus 5.5 under test.
  - Dossiers are blind: arm and hook names are redacted, and successors are mixed with control continuations under a seeded shuffle.
  - Rubrics of checkable claims live in config/lever-rubrics.json.
  - Self-consistency: 20 fixed anchors taken from the D1 hand labels are re-judged in every batch, and 10% of items are re-judged with the order swapped. A batch is void if anchor kappa < 0.8 or swapped-order disagreement > 10%. A void batch is PLUMBING, never a pass.
  - Cap: 40 dossiers a day (estimated at most 0.4 pp/week even at Opus write weight).

6. STAGE LADDER
config/levers.json holds the pre-registration. Its sha is pinned at each stage start, and an edit mid-stage is a PLUMBING verdict.

Common to all levers:
- S0 is the baseline: 7 days of control-only rows, giving a per-event baseline with CI, the A/A false-positive rate (which must sit in [2%, 8%]), and the live MDE.
- The smallest improvement acted on (SIA) must be at least the S2 MDE at the maximum dwell. If it is not, the lever's savings verdict is offline-only.

D3, busy-scoped keepalive with watcher skip (SIA 2.0 pp/week; S3 holdback 5%):
- S0 to S1 needs:
  - at least 7 days of v2+ rows;
  - timer coverage of rebuild gaps at 80% or more (today 47%);
  - A/A OK;
  - the covariate balance test run on S0 pseudo-arms.
- S1 (3-7 days, ends at 20 or more fired wakes) trips on any of:
  - a second wake in the same gap (from any lever);
  - a wake in a headless session;
  - median wake-turn cost above 0.012 pp (twice the measured 0.0060, n=943) once n >= 20;
  - a Wilson lower bound above 30% on the share of wakes that make the model act.
- S2 decides at the looks:
  - ADVANCE iff the fleet pp/week CI lower bound > 0 at that look's bound, the point estimate is at least SIA, the offline replay has the same sign, and the guards are OK.
  - REVERT iff the CI upper bound < 0, or a guard breaches.
  - NOT-MERGED on day 28 if the CI still spans 0.
  - With the timing covariate a day-7 decision is possible (MDE 1.48); context-only needs day 28 (2.85).
- S3: a rolling 28-day check against the holdback (MDE 1.70 with the timing covariate, 6.5 with context only). REVERT iff the holdback CI upper bound < 0.

D4, poll-loop deny (SIA 1.4; holdback 5%):
- Before any stage:
  - the fixed message (a branch for non-wait calls; a repeat-on-124 rule; the pattern widened with `select(undef` and `time.sleep(`);
  - ownership of the 352 calls copied across accounts settled;
  - a re-price at a write weight of 0.20.
- S0 population gate: at least 20 non-exempt poll-loop calls a week. Otherwise PARK and re-check weekly. Today the count is 0.
- S1 is the approved one-day trial: at least 24 h, ending at 10 or more denies, at most 7 days.
  - It trips on any of:
    - 3 or more denies of non-wait calls in 24 h;
    - a Wilson lower bound above 10% on the second-deny rate;
    - a /goal-gate trip after a deny;
    - one agent receiving 3 or more consecutive denies.
  - Compliance: a Wilson lower bound of at least 0.60 on "re-issued as told" (n >= 11 at 90% observed; history is 75%).
- S2 looks: MDE 2.55 / 1.80 / 1.27, and only if the historical 932 calls a week return. ADVANCE iff the CI lower bound > 0, the point estimate is at least 1.4, and the wrong-deny cost is under 0.2% of each account's weekly usage (account is a report stratum here, not an arm).

D2, Workflow block-once (unit is the session):
- S0: 3 days or more of rows after migration 0078; the resume field present; 90% or more of runs joined to their transcripts; σ(log run cost) measured. That σ sets the dwell: at σ 0.8 / 1.2 / 1.6, the cost ratio detectable in 4 weeks is 0.76 / 0.66 / 0.57 (estimated).
- S1 is the approved one-day trial: at least 24 h, ending at 3 treated denies, at most 72 h. Any one of these trips it:
  - a deny on a resume;
  - a deny of a keep-default or needs-default slot;
  - a second deny of the same (sid, sha);
  - any hook timeout or self-bound;
  - p95 latency above 3 s.
- S2 runs until 25 treated denies or 28 days:
  - Advance needs a Wilson lower bound of at least 0.80 on compliance. That takes n >= 16 at 100% observed, 25 at 95%, 54 at 90%.
  - REVERT iff the Wilson upper bound < 0.80 (for example 12 of 20 or 19 of 30).
  - REVERT if the cost log-ratio CI lower bound > 0, meaning lean costs more.
  - Savings: the online CI only if σ allows it, otherwise the offline paired re-gate on held-out production briefs.

D1, idle recycle at 200k after 15 idle min (S3 holdback 10%, kept for calibration):
- S0 is the operator's 7-day fixed shadow (G6), plus a fresh-session replay of 5 successor cases. At most 5 requests and 8k tokens moves conviction up; around 10 requests and 26k holds.
- S1 (at least 3 days, ending at 20 recycles, at most 14 days) trips on any of:
  - one G1 kill or one G4 violation;
  - 2 or more judge-confirmed wrong actions in the first 20 recycles;
  - median successor first turn above 10 requests, or median rework above 10k tokens (the G6 stop rule);
  - 2 or more recycles that do not engage within 10 minutes;
  - any double wake.
- S2 runs until 60 recycles or 28 days. ADVANCE needs all three:
  - the per-recycle net CI lower bound > 0;
  - a fleet-scaled net of at least 4.0 pp/week;
  - the counterfactual within ±25% on control would-advise points.
- S2 also checks:
  - The session-level m2 comparison serves only as a catastrophe check (it resolves 51% or more).
  - The judged re-ask rate: if its Newcombe CI excludes 0 on the harmful side, REVERT.
- Chain accounting (scripts/lib/lever_chain.py): the saving = the sum, over the successor's requests within 24 h, of (the price at the predecessor's context plus the successor's own growth) minus the actual price, less the wake turn, the handoff turn, the orientation excess over the median fresh session, and the priced file-touch rework. The counterfactual comes from w4/sim.py.

Common guards (scorer, at the looks): tool errors per 100 requests excluding hook denials (baseline 2.86; detects a 41% rise), failed lands per land excluding exit 42 (baseline 0.605; 73%), crash rows, and re-asks. A guard breaches when its CI excludes 0 on the harmful side.

Fleet tripwire (daemon): prompt-too-long deaths in treated main sessions, scanned over all four roots: 2 or more a week at S1, 3 or more at S2/S3. False-trip probability: 0.27% at S1; 0.67% at 50% and 4.1% at 100% (Poisson on the 0.087/100 bound).

7. DAEMON: bin/cc-lever-guard
- launchd job com.claude.lever-guard: StartInterval 600, ProcessType Standard, Nice 10, LowPriorityIO. It runs `/bin/bash -c` with an explicit PATH that includes /usr/sbin, then `exec /usr/bin/python3 -I` (the capacity-alarm pattern). Stdlib only; SIGALRM bounds each tick to 60 s; exit codes 0 OK, 1 acted, 2 NO-DATA.
- Each tick:
  1. Touch guard.heartbeat.
  2. If no lever has pct > 0, report IDLE and exit.
  3. Otherwise run `guards` and read the latest score and judge rows.
  4. On a TRIP: demote atomically and latch the trip; write the page ~/.claude/autonomy/pages/lever-<L>.page through page-damp with fingerprint "TRIPPED:<rule>" (operator-readout.sh:348 and cc-escalations read that dir); log a row.
- Blind is not healthy. Two consecutive NO-DATA ticks while pct > 0 demote the lever with rule "blind". NO-DATA means any of: the arm log silent for 6 h while other logs grow, parse errors above 0.5%, unreadable-flag rows, or a scorer timeout.
- If the daemon dies, the dead-man check drops every lever to pct 0 within 30 minutes.
- The daemon never raises a lever, never edits settings, hooks or launchd, and never reverts code. Code goes back by a forward revert through /ship.

8. HILLCLIMB INSIDE THE CANARY
- Only at S2 or S3, one open round per lever, and no round while a trip is un-acked.
- Tier 1 is offline and comes first, because it is the cheapest grader. bin/cc-lever-hillclimb runs over evals built from production:
  - D3: 3,625 gaps in 28 days;
  - D4: 3,730 poll-loop calls;
  - D1: 646 idle points;
  - D2: 275 would-deny runs plus F2's 10 code-graded briefs;
  - plus the canary's train-half events as they accrue.
  - Split: test iff sha1(case_id) % 5 == 0, sealed, stratified by account.
  - Graders are deterministic replays in scripts/lib/lever_replay.py, wrapping sim.py, recompute.py, replay_pred.py/grade.py and cost.py. Each is run twice; any difference is PLUMBING.
- One change per round, aimed at the top root cause from `failures --split train`. Each round is stored under ~/.claude/state/hillclimb/<L>/ as {_state.json, baseline/, vN/{change.md, params.json, results.jsonl, summary.json}, errors.jsonl}.
- Offline accept rule:
  - KEEP iff train delta > 0 and the paired test CI lower bound > 0.
  - Train up but test flat: revert.
  - A regression on either half: revert.
  - 2-3 rounds within noise is a STALL: sort the failures into artifact / grader / harness / structural / variance, and make no edit that round.
- Tier 2 online, only if the offline gain is at least the test-half MDE at 28 days or less. Test-half MDE is:
  - D3 with timing: 2.96 / 2.09 / 1.48;
  - D3 context-only: 11.4 / 8.1 / 5.7;
  - D4: 5.1 / 3.6 / 2.55;
  - D1: never (57 / 41 / 29).
  - The operator runs `cc-lever candidate <L> vN --params .. --share 0.5 --confirm`. Treated units split between incumbent and candidate, and control continues alongside.
  - Decision rule:
    - KEEP iff the test-half CI lower bound > 0, train > 0 and no tripwire fired; then run `cc-lever promote`.
    - Train up but test flat: revert.
    - Either half's CI upper bound < 0: revert.
    - Still within noise at the maximum dwell: NOT-MERGED.
- Leak guard: the analyzer sees train rows only. Text surfaces (deny messages, the wake message, the G3 brief, the G4 regex) must pass leak-check: no 8-gram shared with any train failure.
- What can be tuned:
  - D1: k_thousand, n_min, g4_rx, brief template, lazy_orientation.
  - D2: message, markers.
  - D3: wake_s, max_wakes_per_gap (at most 1 across levers), skip_watcher, min_ctx_k.
  - D4: message, pattern, exempt_inner_lt_s.
- Never tunable: resume pass-through, the headless exemption, one wake per gap, and never auto-rewriting a script.

name: offline-evals-b
design:
OPTION B: OFFLINE EVALS DECIDE, ONLINE TELEMETRY GUARDS

ANSWER FIRST
- Every keep, revert or switch-on verdict comes from offline evals built from production transcripts and scored on a held-out test split.
- Online telemetry only guards: tripwires and a rollback. The measured noise floor puts online MDEs for D1 and D2 at 9 to over 100 times their effects, and D4's at 0.5 to 5 times (noise-floor key), so online data cannot carry the decision for those levers. D3 per-event is the one online confirm within reach, and only at 2-4 weeks.
- Six eval flows:

| Flow | What runs | Grader | Tuned surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| d1-recycle-kn | programmatic replay | programmatic | K, N, G4 |
| d1-successor | model runs | programmatic, then a blind judge | the mechanical brief |
| d2-lean | model runs | answer keys, then a blind judge | lean preamble |
| d3-keepalive | programmatic replay | programmatic | skip rules |
| d4-predicate | programmatic replay | programmatic | poll-loop pattern |
| d4-compliance | model runs | programmatic | deny text |

- They share one kernel, one round driver, and one telemetry substrate (per-unit hash arms with a 20% holdback, a per-session pp ledger, a guard that writes a rollback switch).

Two measurements from this run change the plan:
1. D4's target class is empty today. 0 of 186 v2 subagent rows are would_deny_class=poll-loop. All 37 poll loops carry an inner timeout of 100-270 s and are exempt (measured: python3 -I /tmp/lev-design/offline-evals-b/shadow_now.py). So D4 must pass a headroom check before any round, and may close with "no headroom; do not switch on".
2. The production case pool is about 28 days. ~/.claude-next has 0 main transcripts older than 28 days, against 186 / 1,388 / 1,249 on secondary / tertiary / quaternary (measured: find <root>/projects -maxdepth 2 -name '*.jsonl' -mtime +28 | wc -l). D1 has 71 operator returns at ≥200k context per 14 days (310 points, 196 with a return, 19 context-dependent (H), 10 wrong-action risk (A); measured: python3 -I /tmp/lev-design/offline-evals-b/d1_pool.py).

1. HOW THE BLOG METHOD MAPS HERE
- Production first. Every case comes from real transcripts or live shadow rows; synthetic input appears only as fixtures (D4's file writer).
- Cheapest grader first. Programmatic graders for D1 K/N, D3 and D4. Answer keys checked by code for D2. An LLM judge only for what code cannot see (D1 referent, D2 per-ask completeness).
- Judge rules:
  - The judge is claude-sonnet-5-5; the model under test is claude-opus-5-5.
  - Rubrics are checkable claims, never "which is better".
  - Candidates appear in a seeded random X/Y order with arm names redacted (the collect.py pattern).
  - The judge's JSON parse failure is logged to errors.jsonl as judge-error, never scored.
  - Self-consistency: 20 anchor items are re-judged in every panel with the order swapped. Agreement must be ≥90% and kappa ≥0.8, or the panel is void.
  - Known negatives (empty, "I don't know", an answer to another case) must fail 3/3.
- Plumbing check (`cc-lever-eval check`):
  - Failures are classed from error text only (quota / auth / timeout / served-model / truncated / judge-error) and go to errors.jsonl, re-queued at most 3 times, never scored.
  - The served model is asserted from each transcript's message.model.
  - stop_reason=max_tokens rows become status:truncated.
  - A round whose error rate exceeds 2x baseline or 10% is void.
  - An oracle and a null run through the whole pipeline before round 1.
  - Each replay scorer must reproduce a published number before use (anchors below).
- Baseline with CI. Pp CIs: paired bootstrap, B=2000, clustered by session or case. Rate CIs: Wilson/Newcombe, reusing harness/agg.py:32-70.
- Noise floor below the smallest acted-on change:
  - Model-run flows: NF = the 95% half-width of the paired A/A difference between two baseline reps on the test split.
  - Replays: NF = the bootstrap half-width of a calibration delta.
  - Step 0.5 refuses a round when NF ≥ MIN_ACT.
- Random split: sha1(seed:unit_id) % 2, stratified by tags[0], drawn once. Train and test baseline means must agree within NF, else re-draw.
- One change per round, targeting a root cause.
- Accept rule, encoded in hc.decide(), applies at both read-weight ends:
  - REVERT if any hold breaches its margin on either split.
  - REVERT if train or test falls below −NF.
  - KEEP if train > NF_train and test CI95 lower bound > 0.
  - REVERT as overfit if train > NF but test CI includes 0.
  - Otherwise REVERT (flat). Three non-KEEP rounds in a row = STALL.
  - On STALL: an analyzer sorts the train failures into artifact / grader / harness / structural / variance and writes the counts to vN/change.md, with no edit that round.
  - Train down with test up counts as noise: append reps and keep only if it repeats.
- Isolation and leaks:
  - The analyzer is a fresh subagent handed only train trace paths, train result rows and the train rows of scores.tsv. The lead never reads traces.
  - Leak check: `cc-hillclimb round` refuses a patch whose added lines share any 8-word n-gram with any case text (operator prompts, briefs, command heads).
- Harness gate (ported from runner-scaffold.mjs): the sha over harness_paths must match the one recorded by the operator's `--approve-harness`.
- Report: test winner vs baseline with CI. A gain whose CI includes 0 is reported as "do not merge".

2. TELEMETRY SUBSTRATE (guard plane; also prices every model-run eval)

Arms: hooks/lib/lever_arm.py
- arm(lever, unit) = "treat" if int(sha256(f"{SALT}:{lever}:{unit}")[:8], 16) % 100 < PCT, else "hold".
- SALT = CC_LEVER_SALT (default "lev-2026-10-24"). Each lever hashes separately, so the four splits are orthogonal (factorial) and each guard reads alone.
- Unit per lever:
  - D1: chain-root sid. The brief carries the marker "[idle-recycle chain=<root-sid>]", and chain_root() reads it from the successor's first user record.
  - D2: session sid.
  - D3: sid + ":" + gap_start (per event).
  - D4: agent_id (per agent, so a learned deny does not leak across arms).
- Arms are stateless; every lever row logs arm, and the ledger recomputes it. A mismatch trips T8.
- No SessionStart edit is needed.

Flags
- Lever modes, read by lever_arm.mode(lever): CC_IDLE_RECYCLE=shadow|enforce|off (new), CC_WORKFLOW_LEAN=shadow|block-once|off (new; CC_WORKFLOW_SHADOW stays the logging switch), CC_IDLE_KEEPALIVE=shadow|enforce|off, CC_SUBAGENT_LONG_BASH=shadow|enforce|off.
- Treatment shares: CC_IDLE_RECYCLE_PCT, CC_WORKFLOW_LEAN_PCT, CC_IDLE_KEEPALIVE_PCT, CC_SUBAGENT_LONG_BASH_PCT, each default 80.
- D1 parameters: CC_IDLE_RECYCLE_K (thousands, default 200), CC_IDLE_RECYCLE_N_MIN (default 15, hard cap 55 per the W4 learning).
- D3 parameters: CC_KEEPALIVE_SCOPE=busy|any (default busy), CC_KEEPALIVE_WATCHER_SKIP=1, CC_KEEPALIVE_MIN_CTX_K=0, plus the existing CC_KEEPALIVE_WAKE_S=3300 and CC_KEEPALIVE_MAX_WAKES=1.
- Mode precedence: env off > state file ~/.claude/state/levers/<lever>.json {mode, pct, set_by, ts} > env mode > default shadow.
- The state file is read on every hook call, so a change reaches live sessions at once, unlike env, which reaches only new sessions.
- It is written only by `cc-lever-guard --set` (operator, any mode) or `--rollback` (guard, downgrade to shadow only). Rollback is therefore one command with no c10 settings edit; promotion stays an operator act.

Ledger: bin/cc-lever-ledger
- Imports bin/cc-token-ledger scan() (:416) and trees() (:552) via SourceFileLoader, which keeps its message.id dedupe, earliest-file copy rule and output imputation.
- Prices quota pp at read 0.0067 (range 0.0057-0.0076), write 0.245, output 0.404.
- Joins:
  - land.log ship-land rows by sid (exit 0 = ok; exits 6/5/11/143 = failed; 42 = internal re-rebase, excluded, as in the noise-floor key)
  - backlog done rows by closedSession
  - claude-crashes.jsonl
  - "Prompt is too long" deaths (via cc-ctx-audit, after its roots fix)
  - the four lever logs
- Excludes eval sessions: any project key starting -private-tmp-lev-eval or -tmp-lev-eval is labelled eval and kept out of arm contrasts, but stays in fleet totals.
- `--by-arm dN` prints treat vs hold with a session-bootstrap CI and the MDE line beside it, so "clear" reads as "no regression larger than X".

Guard: bin/cc-lever-guard (section 5).

Plumbing fix the guard depends on: bin/cc-ctx-audit:72-74 omits ~/.claude-secondary/projects, the root that held all 3 of the week's prompt-too-long transcripts; its 7-day run also timed out at 240 s (telemetry-inventory key).

3. EVAL KERNEL AND DRIVER

tools/lever-evals/lib/hc.py implements the bundled SCHEMA v2 layout under ~/.claude/hillclimb/<flow>/ (outside git, because cases hold private operator text):
- _state.json: goal {target, direction, hold[]}, train_ids, test_ids, split_seed, reps, harness_paths, harness_sha, metrics, perf_fields [pp_mid, requests, latency_s], best {round, test_score}, noise_floor {train, test, method}, min_act, fingerprint {repo_sha, claude_bin, model, effort, weights}, looks
- metrics.md, narrative.md
- baseline/ and vN/, each holding change.md, change.patch (against real repo paths), params.json, results.jsonl, errors.jsonl, summary.json, traces/<id>_rep<k>.json, decision.json
- trajectory/scores.tsv

results.jsonl row: {prompt_id, rep, tags[stratum, acct], grade{...}, explanation{...}, model, judge_model, usage, judge_usage, pp{lo, mid, hi}, requests, latency_s, status, meta{fixture_sha, arm, case_window}}.

A fingerprint change forces a re-baseline. Model runs execute arm A then arm B (ABBA order) on one account per block, so the account is never an arm (sched.py rule), and pause an account at 85% weekly (STOP_PCT). Reports are rendered by a vendored copy of the bundled build-report-lite.mjs.

bin/cc-hillclimb:
- init: goal, holds, MIN_ACT, reps
- round: one change, then apply, run, score, decide, rewrite narrative.md and its status table, rebuild the report; exit 0 KEEP / 1 REVERT / 4 STALL / 3 void
- status
- report: final test vs baseline with CI and the number of test looks

The runner is a single background Bash call per the guide. Replay flows apply a params.json change instead of a patch.

4. FLOWS

MIN_ACT values:
- Every pp target: 1.0 pp/week fleet. That is about 0.25% of the ~400 pp/week capacity; W3's 0.2% bar is 0.8, rounded up.
- d1-successor pass rate: 5 points.
- d2-lean pass rate and d4-compliance rate: 10 points.

d1-recycle-kn (programmatic)
- What it is: tools/lever-evals/d1_recycle/sim.py, a port of docs/research/usage-levers-2026-10-23/w4/sim.py.
- Parameters: k, n_min, g1 busy-by-launching-tool, g4 phrase classes (session_jobs.pending_question at hooks/lib/session_jobs.py:208).
- Data: 28 days of main sessions, all accounts, with per-session output.
- Score: net pp/week = gross saving − successor first turn (measured by d1-successor, not the W4 median) − handoff turn (0 for a mechanical brief) − jobs moved to the background − G4 hold.
- Hold: projected wrong actions per week = Σ over eligible returns of P(wrong | case) from d1-successor rows. K/N rounds re-weight the stored rows, so they need no model runs.
- Anchor: on the same 14-day window, reproduce gross 16.36 (150k/15) and 15.39 (200k/15) pp/week within ±5% (measured: rp90.out, decisions REPORT).
- Split: by chain-root sid, stratified by account.
- NF: bootstrap half-width of a 25k K step. If NF ≥ 1.0, step by 50k.
- Search space: K 150-300 step 25; N 10-30 step 5.

d1-successor (model runs; tunes hooks/lib/idle_recycle_brief.py)
- The brief is mechanical and doubles as production D1's brief, so the eval regenerates exactly what production sends. It holds:
  - G3: the final message verbatim, open questions, handed-over steps, the transcript path, watchers and Monitors to re-arm
  - the chain marker
  - G5 lazy orientation and the "ask if a short reply matches more than one item" rule
- Cases: operator returns that end an idle gap of ≥10 min at ≥150k context, over 28 days, with tags[0] = H/S/I/A.
  - All H and A cases plus a random S/I sample, about 200 in all (100 train / 100 test; estimated by doubling the 14-day counts).
  - Existing labels are imported first from /tmp/idle-recycle-risk/b and /tmp/conv-tests/43da49891e75: 60 + 133 labels, the second labeller's 60 (kappa 1.00/0.88) and the 10 replays.
  - New cases are labelled by a Sonnet 5.5 labeller that must reach kappa ≥0.8 against the 60 double-labelled cases.
- Fixture:
  - git archive of origin/main at the idle time
  - the predecessor transcript truncated at the idle point (the future never enters the fixture)
  - the machine inputs between the idle point and the return
