How trips are judged:
- A trip needs a one-sided p < 0.05, Holm-corrected across the active triggers, on the treat-vs-hold contrast.
- An 80/20 split inflates MDEs 1.25x over 50/50 (estimated: sqrt(6.25/4)).

Triggers:
- T1 tool errors without hook denies, treat/hold, ≥7 days. MDE about 51% (41% at 50/50, measured noise-floor).
- T2 failed ship-land per land. MDE about 91% (73% at 50/50).
- T3 count alarm: ≥3 prompt-too-long main deaths in treatment per week (p ≈ 0.04 at the rule-of-three bound).
- T4 D1:
  - ≥10 live recycles with a median first turn > 10 requests, or rework > 10k tokens
  - or ≥2 wrong actions in the first 20 recycles, confirmed by a correction regex pre-filter plus a Sonnet judge
- T5 D2: edited-resubmit rate < 80% over ≥10 blocks; any block on a resume; a slot failure ratio > 1.5.
- T6 D3: over ≥20 live wakes, a median > 3 requests or > 0.012 pp per wake (2x the measured median), or an acting share 10 points above the replay's assumption.
- T7 D4: second-deny > 10%; re-issue-as-told < 60%; wrong-deny cost > 0.2% of weekly per account.
- T8 plumbing: weekly meter/wpp outside [1.1, 1.5] (measured fleet range 1.20-1.36), or a logged arm ≠ the recomputed arm, or eval rows found in production. T8 freezes decisions; it does not roll back.

Actions:
- A trip runs `--rollback <lever>`, which sets the state file to shadow.
- Continue = no trip over the window: 1 day, then 7 days at 80/20 for D2 and D4; 7 days for D1 and D3. Then the operator runs `cc-lever-guard --set dN enforce --pct 100`.
- D3 only: a 4-week online confirm is possible, with MDE about 5.0/3.5 pp/week at 2/4 weeks (estimated by 1.25x scaling of the measured 4.0/2.8).

D1's prior labels, replays and the D2/D3/D4 intermediates live only in /tmp (/tmp/idle-recycle-risk/b, /tmp/conv-tests). A reboot loses them. W14 must copy them into ~/.claude/hillclimb before anything else. This run did not copy them, because the brief allowed writes only under /tmp/lev-design/<key>/.

Eval spend is real quota: about 40-50 pp for baselines plus about 3 rounds per model-run flow (estimated from cost.out per-slot means and the 43.8k re-prime), roughly 10-12% of one week's ~400 pp. Run it on accounts with headroom, with the 85% stop.

Fixture fidelity. Successors run with --setting-sources project, so SessionStart context injections (about 2.5k chars) and hooks are missing. A git archive of origin/main differs from the session's worktree state. Reads of live ~/.claude stores would leak the future, so the capture hook confines reads to the fixture. The ±15% first-request wiring check is the guard.

Eval runs write transcripts into the real accounts' projects dirs, and shadow hooks would log them if user settings loaded. That pollutes the token ledger and the shadow logs. Mitigations: the /tmp/lev-eval cwd-key exclusion, CC_WORKFLOW_SHADOW=off and log redirects in eval leads, and the T8 tripwire.

The judge (Sonnet 5.5) is the same family as Opus 5.5, so self-preference is reduced but not removed. Calibrating against human labels needs about 20 operator-labelled pairs (operator time). Without them, the judge stays secondary to the programmatic metrics.

pp claims rest on the brief's weights: write 0.245 from a fit, read 0.0057-0.0076, a possible long-context premium above 200k (round-3 confound), and a 1h write premium (2.8% likely). The read range is carried into every KEEP. D4 gets a write-0.20 sensitivity check. The meter/wpp calibration tripwire is the backstop.

Unverified mechanics: whether a headless `claude -p` lead waits for Workflow completion, and whether --agents or a fixture project agent overrides the user-level workflow-lean for agentType. The rule that agent definitions are cached at session start means each round needs a fresh process. Fallback: run the D2/D4 Workflows from an interactive eval lead.

The online guard detects only large regressions: tool errors about 51%, failed lands about 91% relative at 80/20 (estimated, 1.25x the measured 50/50 MDEs). D1 and D2 can never be confirmed online, so a mis-specified offline eval would go unnoticed. Every 'clear' line prints its MDE.

Automatic rollback through the state file is a new control path. False trips are bounded by Holm correction across T1-T8. T3 and T4 are hard alarms. Promotion stays an operator command. A wrong guard still reverts a good change until the operator re-sets it.

Arm contamination. A D1 successor inherits its arm only through the chain marker in the brief; a lost marker gives an independent arm. The T8 logged-vs-recomputed check catches it. Per-agent D4 arms still let one session hold both arms.

Repeated test looks on deterministic replays (D3, D1 K/N, D4 predicate) invite forking-paths overfit to the test split. Mitigations: cap at 6 rounds per flow, record looks in _state.json, and confirm the final winner on the 7 days after the loop before switch-on.

Platform drift mid-loop (the 2.1.293 pin, model or effort changes, the agentsync b13 loop starting or stopping) breaks comparability. The fingerprint in _state.json forces a re-baseline; control re-runs gate against drift.

D1's design assumes a mechanical brief, so the eval regenerates production's brief exactly. If implementers instead wake the predecessor to write it via /handoff, d1-successor needs a fork arm (claude -p --resume --fork-session), estimated at 0.05-0.25 pp per case (200k-1M context write at 0.245 pp/Mtok).

scores.name: option-a-session-ab
scores.note: Statistically the most careful of the three, but it picked the weakest randomization unit. It measured the design effect and has a strong plumbing gate: SRM per account, placebo A/A, logged vs recomputed arm, an exposure floor of 80%, KS/SMD balance, CR1 vs bootstrap within 20%, and CIs taken as the union over both read-weight ends. The problem is that it randomizes every lever by lineage. Its own cluster_mde.out (I re-read it) shows what that costs. D3 needs 8.82 pp/wk to be detected at 4 weeks under lineage randomization, against 3.01 if each gap is randomized, and the expected effect is only 3.9-5.1. For D4 the figures are 8.12 vs 1.34. So D3 can only be decided if the return-timing covariate (R2 0.942) passes the balance check. That covariate may be moved by the treatment itself, for example a wake that brings the operator back sooner. If balance fails, the design itself says the verdict is STALL. D1 and D2 savings are modelled per recycle, and nothing checks the counterfactual against the control arm. D4 is MOOT: in my count (python over the last 400 subagent-long-bash rows) there were 0 would-deny poll-loop v2 rows and 51 exempted by inner timeout. Rollback: the control files are read on every hook call, an unreadable file falls back to shadow and raises an alarm, an ack is needed to re-enable, and env clamps can only lower. But the tick is hourly and there is no dead-man switch once a round is running; the heartbeat is checked only at round-start. Cost: about 990K output tokens over 11 waves, plus a launchd job and a c10 migration. Fidelity: the accept rule, the sealed test half and the cause-sorted failures follow the method. But the evals are mostly online, with production-replay graders used only as a pre-flight. The train/test halves of live traffic also widen each half's MDE by sqrt2.

scores.name: offline-evals-b
scores.note: The closest to the blog. Cases come from production transcripts, programmatic graders come first, the judge (Sonnet) is a different model from the one tested and works from checkable claims in blind order, 20 anchors are re-judged each panel with kappa of at least 0.8, oracle and null runs plus truncation and served-model checks cover the plumbing, rounds are refused when the noise floor is at or above MIN_ACT, the split is stratified by hash, there is an 8-gram leak check and a harness-sha gate, and decide() encodes the accept rule exactly. Measurement validity is weaker than that suggests. Inside the eval, the offline flows separate + from - easily, but most of the D3, D1-K/N and D4 replays price outcomes with the same cost model (idle_gap.py, w4/sim.py) that produced the expected effects, so they partly re-derive the claim. The anchor checks verify the code, not the model. d1-successor is the one real behavioural measurement of side costs, and its fixtures lack SessionStart context; the +/-15% wiring probe is only a partial guard. In production, D1 and D2 are never confirmed, and the guards only catch large regressions: about 51% for tool errors and about 91% for failed lands at 80/20. The optional D3 online confirm has an MDE of about 3.5 at 4 weeks (estimated) against 3.9-5.1 expected, which is marginal. Rollback is a downgrade-only state file read on every hook call, with Holm-corrected trips, and offline gates must pass before any switch-on. But the default treatment share is 80% from day one, there is no dead-man switch, and the guard's launchd registration is a c10 step. This is the most expensive design: about 1.1-1.6M tokens over 12 waves, plus 40-50 pp of eval quota (about 10-12% of a week, per the design's own estimate) and unverified headless Workflow/--agents mechanics.

scores.name: option-c-staged-canary
scores.note: The best measurement validity of the three. Randomizing D3 per gap, with CIs clustered by session, keeps the lever decidable even without the timing covariate. stage_mde.out (re-read) gives a context-only MDE of 2.85 pp/wk at 4 weeks at 50%, below the 3.9 low end of the expected effect. Haybittle-Peto bounds the interim looks, and the pre-registration is sha-pinned. An A/A false-positive rate must fall in 2-8% before anything advances. It is the only design that checks the D1 counterfactual against control-arm points (within +/-25%). D3 can ADVANCE only if the offline replay agrees in sign. The plumbing block compares join coverage and imputed-output share between arms. D4 is held at a population gate (PARK), and S1 at 10% is honestly labelled as tripwire and compliance only. Two flaws. First, its claim that D3 can be decided at day 7 with MDE 1.48 ignores its own |z|>=3.0 interim bound; that bound gives about 2.0 (estimated: 1.48 x 3.84/2.80), which is still under 3.9. Second, D1 and D2 savings remain modelled or offline. Rollback is the strongest of the three: a 30-minute dead-man switch, ticks every 10 minutes, trips that latch and need an ack, blind ticks count as a demote, an unreadable file reads as pct 0, the guard can only lower, cohorts are nested starting from 10%, and raises are behind ask rules. Cost: about 0.9-1.2M tokens over 8 waves, plus a launchd daemon, two c10 migrations, rotation and store-bounds edits, and edits on the risky 20k-line handoff-fire.sh. Fidelity: it does the offline-first programmatic production replays, the sealed sha1%5 split, the leak check and the STALL sort. But it has fewer model-run evals mirroring production (no D1 successor-behaviour eval), and KEEP needs only train delta > 0, not train above noise.

scores.name: option-a-session-ab
offline-evals-b
scores.note:
Option B follows the blog most closely.
- Cases come from production transcripts, and graders are programmatic first.
- Every replay scorer must reproduce a published number before use, and oracle and null runs go through the pipeline.
- It refuses a round when the noise floor reaches MIN_ACT.
- The judge is Sonnet, not the tested model, with anchors, kappa and known negatives.
- The split is stratified and its halves must balance; it changes one thing per round.
- decide() encodes the accept rule, the analyzer sees train cases only, an 8-gram leak check guards the tuned surface, and a harness-sha gate is required.
Detection: the deterministic replays (D1 K/N, D3, the D4 predicate) give tight CIs. The model-run flows are small (d2-lean 20/20, d1-successor about 100/100), so their CIs are wide. The 5-point noise floor for d1-successor at R=2 looks optimistic (estimated: a Wilson half-width at n=100 is about 10 points). Online, realized net impact is never measured for D1, D2 and D4. Guards at an 80/20 split resolve only about 51% (tool errors) and 91% (failed lands), and Holm correction across T1-T8 dilutes them further.
Rollback is the weakest of the three. Promotion goes straight to 80% treatment, so the one-day D2 and D4 trials also run at 80%. There is no dead-man switch, no trip latch with ack, and T8 freezes decisions without rolling back. Guard cadence depends on a c10 launchd step. Offline gating before any exposure is a real safety gain, but eval runs write into the real accounts' projects dirs, so they need exclusion. It is the most expensive option: about 1.1-1.6M tokens over 12 waves (design estimate), plus 40-50 pp of eval quota (10-12% of a week). It also depends on unverified mechanics: whether a headless lead waits for a Workflow to finish, and whether --agents overrides the user-level agent.

scores.name: option-c-staged-canary
scores.note:
Option C has the strongest rollback design.
- A dead-man switch drops every lever to pct 0 if the guard heartbeat is older than 1800 s.
- The guard can only lower a lever, and a trip latches until the operator acks it.
- Two NO-DATA ticks demote the lever, so a blind guard is never treated as healthy.
- An unreadable flags file gives pct 0.
- Cohorts nest (10% inside 50% inside 100%), so no unit flips arm; the salt rotates after a trip.
- The thresholds sha is pinned at each stage start.
- Raises need --confirm, an ADVANCE verdict and ask rules; first exposure is 10%, with S3 holdbacks.
- The tick runs every 10 min, bounded to 60 s by SIGALRM, and the plist is tested under /bin/bash 3.2, as the repo rule requires.
- It adds the shadow logs to rotation and store-bounds. Measured: a grep of config/store-bounds.manifest and scripts/rotate-autonomy-logs.sh found none of the four logs today.
Detection: units are per event (a D3 gap, a D4 agent), which gives better online power than A. Pre-registration, Haybittle-Peto looks, an S0 A/A that measures the false-positive rate, and a rule sending a lever offline-only when its SIA is below the MDE are all sound. But the D4 MDEs in stage_mde.out (2.55/1.80/1.27) assume randomization per call, while assignment is per agent_id with CIs clustered by session. A's measured session design effect for D4 (27-37) says those figures are optimistic. The rule also allows SIA equal to the MDE. S1 at 10% carries no savings information, which the design admits.
Risks: edits to handoff-fire.sh, and toil from false demotions. idle-keepalive is a Stop hook with a 14400 s timeout (measured: python scan of ~/.claude/settings.json), so the flags must be re-read at the due time; the design does this ('at each due time'). Build cost is about 0.8-1.05M tokens over 8 waves (design estimate), plus two c10 migrations. The top migration today is 0078 (ls migrations), so 0079 and 0080 are free.
